title: Make every hreflang cluster reciprocal and self-referential
statement: Each page in a locale set lists every member of that set including itself, and each page it names lists it back, so no member of the cluster points outward without a return declaration.
rationale: A one-directional annotation is discarded rather than partially honoured, so a cluster with one missing return link loses the association for the whole set rather than for one page.
implementation: Generate the whole annotation set from one locale table shared by every page in the cluster, rather than letting each template emit the alternates it happens to know about. Emit the self reference from the same loop that emits the others.

verification.method: Fetch every page in each locale cluster, build the directed graph of declared alternates, and report members missing a self reference or a return edge.

caution: Editing cluster membership changes which locale is served to which audience, so the change is reviewed rather than applied automatically even though the defect is mechanical.

title: Express locale codes as valid language tags
statement: Every locale identifier the site emits is a well-formed language tag, using a registered language subtag and, where a region is meant, a registered region subtag rather than an invented abbreviation.
rationale: An unregistered tag such as a country name where a language subtag belongs is not interpreted as a near miss, so the annotation carrying it is dropped rather than approximated.
implementation: Hold the tag for each locale once as a validated constant and derive every emission from it, so a URL segment, a document attribute, and an annotation cannot disagree. Validate the tags against the subtag registry during the build.

verification.method: Collect every locale identifier from served documents and annotations and parse each against the language-tag grammar and the registered subtag lists.

title: Keep each locale page canonical to itself rather than to another locale
statement: A translated page declares itself as its own canonical, and no locale variant is consolidated onto a different locale, so the cluster keeps one indexable page per language.
rationale: Pointing a translation at the original locale asks for the two to be treated as one page, which withdraws the translation from the index and defeats the reason it was published.
implementation: Derive the canonical value from the locale-qualified route rather than from a default-locale route constant, and reserve cross-locale consolidation for pages that genuinely duplicate an existing locale word for word.

verification.method: Request each locale route and compare its served canonical value against its own address, reporting any that resolves to a different locale.

caution: The cited documentation describes cross-locale annotation and consolidation as separate mechanisms; treating one as a substitute for the other is the defect this record detects.

title: Let every locale URL be reachable without an automatic redirect
statement: A request for a specific locale address returns that locale, whatever the requesting address or declared preferences suggest, and any locale suggestion is offered as a link the reader can decline.
rationale: A client that is redirected away from the address it asked for never sees that locale, so a site that reroutes by inferred region publishes translations no requester outside that region can reach.
implementation: Replace inferred rerouting on locale-qualified paths with a dismissible suggestion, and confine automatic locale selection to the bare root path where no locale was requested.

verification.method: Request each locale address from varied source regions and preference headers and report any that answers with a redirect to a different locale.

caution: Removing established rerouting alters where existing readers land, so the change is staged and reviewed rather than applied in one pass.

title: Declare x-default only for a genuine fallback page
statement: The unspecified-locale annotation names a page built to serve requesters no other locale matches, and is absent when the site has no such page rather than defaulting to whichever locale was written first.
rationale: Nominating an ordinary locale as the fallback sends every unmatched requester to a page written for a different audience, which is worse than declaring no fallback at all.
implementation: Decide once whether a locale-neutral entry page exists, record that decision in the locale table, and emit the annotation from the recorded decision rather than from a template default.

verification.method: Collect the unspecified-locale annotation across each cluster and confirm it names the page the locale table designates as locale-neutral, or is absent where none is designated.

caution: Whether a locale-neutral page exists is an editorial fact about the site, so this process reports a doubtful designation instead of choosing one.

title: Exclude untranslated pages from the locale cluster
statement: A locale route that returns source-language text because no translation exists is left out of the annotation set, so the cluster describes only the pages actually rendered in the language they claim.
rationale: A route that answers in the wrong language while declaring another one misdescribes itself, and a reader who follows the declaration arrives at text they cannot read.
implementation: Have the translation layer report which locales a given page exists in, and build the annotation set from that report rather than from the list of locales the site supports overall.

verification.method: Compare the rendered body language of each annotated locale route against the language it declares and report routes where the two disagree.

caution: This asserts only that a declaration should match what the route returns, which is an internal consistency property needing no external citation. Whether a partial translation is worth publishing is an editorial decision left to the site.
